content.text:
I submitted **index 23 (Sb 0.82, Zn 0.18)** as the best composition. It had the highest EQE of my three measurements, though every value was very low (below 0.01%).

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0.66 (ZnSb₂O₆ composition) | about 0 (−0.00008) |
| 29 | 0.90 | 0.0015 |
| **23** | **0.82** | **0.0076** |

- **Why these three:** MEGNet predicts small band gaps (0.05–0.5 eV) for the Sb-rich phases ZnSb₄O₈ and ZnSb₄O₉, meaning they should absorb the 2.4 eV light. Its prediction for ZnSb₂O₆ is 1.97 eV, but that seemed too low against the reported experimental value of about 3.4 eV. Index 16 then measured essentially zero. So I moved to the Sb-rich end, and the Gaussian-process model ranked index 23 top for the last measurement.
- **XRD didn't help:** I used 3 of the 5 XRD scans (indices 3, 16, 27). No reference phase matched well; the best similarity was 0.33. So I couldn't tell which phases are actually in the film.
- **Not tested:** the Zn-rich half of the library (Sb below 0.6), apart from the one XRD scan at index 3. I assumed it is wide-gap ZnO and spinel that won't absorb at 2.4 eV, but that is a guess rather than a measurement. The neighbours of index 23 (indices 21–25) were also left unmeasured, so the true best may sit next to it.
